kept.reason: Checks that each failed store call (Claim, Renew, DeadLetters, ...) reaches the worker as Error::Store with that call's error. a_worker_claims_heartbeats_and_finishes_a_task checks the happy path of claim, heartbeat and finish: no assertion there injects a store error, and the flaky per-call loop would change what it checks. No assertion maps; the setups conflict.

Checks that starting a process again with the same key and other input is refused key_reused, and after it ends is refused ended, with the call made once. a_process_runs_to_completion checks only completion, status paid and one charge under the step's key: none of its assertions checks a second start. Folding the restart assertions into it would put two guarantees in one scenario, against lib.rs's one home per guarantee, and hide which one failed; it would save under 10ms of world setup.

Checks that a checkout over LIMIT ends Failed(declined) and its order is compensated to cancelled. a_process_runs_to_completion checks a checkout under the limit completes and is paid: no assertion maps, and the setups conflict (one amount is declined, the other charged), so one test cannot hold both.

kept_files.reason: Deep already: four public task calls (claim_task, heartbeat, finish_task, cancel_task) and five crate entries tick calls (advance_due, deliver, run_due, expire_waits, arrived) hide leases, retry/at-most-once, key pacing, lost-race retry and wait-before-row answers. Every row kind runs through one claim/drain loop and ends through one end_attempt/answer_step path; fault naming lives in item(). Tests cross only the engine API. Splitting by row kind would move lines, not add depth; remaining smells (answer_step's 7 args, a repeated Step::Await rebuild in advance_one) are local and small.

Deep already: programs write typed traits (Aggregate, Command, Process, Projection) and the engine holds erased Dyn* forms by name through three constructors (aggregate_of, command_of, process_of), which hide serde tag/data encoding, upcasting by version, state decoding and the fault-vs-rejection split. Retry is one home (factum#23): the engine asks only on_claim and after_failure, never re-derives Unknown/Failed or backoff. All 90-day churn was that retry rule settling (#23, #30), not a shallow seam. Moving the policies beside Work in work.rs would move lines, not add depth; the rest (Recurring::period_start, RowOp, OnFailure) is small declaration data.

Deep enough after its splits: the 23 commits in 90 days are mostly the moves that already deepened it (schema.rs factum#48, tables.rs and work.rs factum#57, checkpoints into tables.rs factum#68), taking it from 813 to 257 prod lines. What remains is open/path plus the Store trait (SPEC §3), a seam with two adapters; the per-call methods are the trait's adapter bodies (marshal args onto the connection thread, one immediate transaction per write), not pass-throughs, and the events log and snapshots SQL left here are this file's own concern. Rules every store shares already live in factum-store; tests cross only the engine API. Splitting the events log into its own module would move lines, not add depth.

Still deep, and smaller than at its last keep (746 -> 653 prod lines): the same 8 public calls (submit, plan, state, history, start, process, tick, settle) hide idempotent replay by key and fingerprint, race retry (Races, ADR 0017), snapshots, upcasting, the ending check and dispatch; every event still goes through the one private write()/unit(). The 9 commits since were behaviour changes behind that interface (factum#39-43 runner outcomes and refusals, #70 serialization, #78 doc rehome), not one concept spreading. Tests reach it only through conformance scenarios. What is left is small and internal (process_state, a one-line pass-through over process_events; record's 7 args, used 3 times), not worth a change.
